newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina Faso budget approved, help for farmers.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso budget approved, help for farmers.

text.p: Burkina Faso's parliament has approved a 1997 budget with a lower deficit than in 1996 and a special contribution to help farmers buy fertiliser and pesticides.
The budget, approved late on Friday despite "No" votes from the opposition, projects spending of 397.4 billion CFA francs, up 10.2 percent on 1996.
With projected government revenue up 15.5 percent, the projected deficit falls from 38.9 billion CFA to just over 25 billion CFA or 1.86 percent of Gross Domestic Product.
Officials said that the government aimed to plug the gap by improving collection of taxes, curbing spending and with the help of the West African nation's development partners.
The budget includes a special allocation of 1.2 billion CFA to help with farm inputs.

Burkina Faso has a programme to boost farm production with the aim of self-sufficiency. Cereal production this year was in surplus. Insect damage cut output of cotton -- a major export -- to 180,000 tonnes from an expected 200,000 tonnes.
The budget, for the first time, also introduces subsidies for political parties, the private press and a consumer group.
